en.summary: South Korea has a fast, highly digital news market where most people read news through portals run by Naver and Kakao. Three large dailies, the Chosun Ilbo, JoongAng Ilbo and Dong-A Ilbo, have long dominated print, while the Hankyoreh, founded with citizen shareholders, and the employee-owned Kyunghyang Shinmun offer alternative ownership models. Public broadcasters KBS and MBC sit alongside commercial channels SBS, JTBC and the 24-hour news channel YTN. Yonhap, the national news agency, receives public funding. Investigative reporting is produced by broadcasters, a weekly magazine and Newstapa, a nonprofit newsroom funded by members. Business newspapers are numerous, reflecting the weight of conglomerates in the economy. Regional newspapers serve Busan, Daegu, Gyeonggi and Gangwon.

faq.q: What are the main national news outlets in South Korea?
faq.a: The main national outlets in the directory include Yonhap News Agency, The Chosun Ilbo, JoongAng Ilbo, The Dong-A Ilbo and The Hankyoreh. The Top National News column lists them in editorial order.

faq.q: Which South Korean news sites are free to read?
faq.a: Free-to-read outlets include Yonhap News Agency, The Chosun Ilbo, The Dong-A Ilbo, The Hankyoreh and Kyunghyang Shinmun. The paywall model of every outlet is shown next to its name.

faq.q: Which South Korean outlets are publicly or state funded?
faq.a: Public-service outlets include Yonhap News Agency, KBS News and MBC News. Ownership is labeled on every outlet in the directory.

faq.q: Where can I find regional news in South Korea?
faq.a: Regional coverage in the directory comes from Busan Ilbo (Busan), Kookje Shinmun (Busan), Maeil Shinmun (Daegu), Kyeongin Ilbo (Gyeonggi) and Kangwon Ilbo (Gangwon). The Regional & Local column lists every regional outlet.

general-news.intro: National news in South Korea comes from the Yonhap agency, national dailies with different ownership models and an English-language daily. Paywall model and owner are shown for each outlet.

economy.intro: South Korean business journalism follows conglomerates, semiconductors, real estate and the stock market through several dedicated business dailies.

sports.intro: Sports media in South Korea covers KBO baseball, K League football and golf through sports dailies linked to national newspaper groups and fast online outlets.

broadcast.intro: Broadcast news in South Korea includes two public broadcasters, a commercial terrestrial network, cable news channels and a 24-hour news channel.

regional.intro: Regional newspapers in South Korea cover Busan, Daegu, Gyeonggi Province and Gangwon Province.

politics.intro: Political coverage in South Korea follows the presidency, the National Assembly and party politics through national dailies, the national news agency and digital outlets.
